title: Short-Form Vertical Video for Digital Activism
summary: Six formats, one structure (Hook → Core → Call to Action) and the platform rules you need to turn a message into a video people don't scroll past.
description: A practical, hands-on guide to using short-form vertical video for civic engagement, political commentary and social activism. It explains why vertical video has become the dominant format, and how its full-screen orientation creates immediacy, urgency and authenticity.

Participants analyse a full taxonomy of short-form styles: "boomer car rants", multi-persona dialogues, satire, video essays and vox populi interviews. They learn practical strategies including the "Lookout Mindset", trend-jacking, steelmanning counter-arguments, and scripts built on the Hook → Core → Call to Action framework.
The lesson covers psychological tactics such as memes as Trojan horses for complex or radical ideas, persona building, and using confrontation to increase shareability.

Finally, it covers the technical logistics: platform specs for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, publishing best practices, safety warnings, and how to avoid algorithmic censorship or shadowbanning on sensitive political topics.

variants.text: Focus only on the video taxonomy and the Hook → Core → Call to Action structure. Skip the storyboarding exercise.
Extend the group activity into a live workshop: groups record and edit a raw 60-second vertical draft on their phones, followed by a class screening.

Respect platform limits and caption zones, and avoid safety hazards and algorithmic penalties on sensitive topics
targetGroup: Young creators, digital activists, NGO workers, communications students and civic organisers who want to turn social and political messages into engaging short-form video.

steps.title: The vertical revolution
bullets: **The mobile context:** social media went from static to video, and over 90% of social media consumption happens on mobile.
**Portrait vs. landscape:** orientation is a friction barrier. Vertical video takes 100% of the screen and feels intimate, urgent and raw.
**A call to creators:** "The world is run by those who show up." Post consistently on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube Shorts.

steps.title: Taxonomy of short-form video formats
body: Six formats, each with a different production effort and strategic advantage:

formats.name: Monologue rant
formats.text: Direct to camera (e.g. "boomer car rants"). Very authentic and fast to make, but audiences tire of it.

formats.name: Dialogue
formats.text: One creator plays two personas looking off-camera. Great for tackling talking points and counter-arguments in a controlled, fun way.

formats.name: Sketch & satire
formats.text: High viral potential. Humour disarms prejudice.

formats.name: Video essay / explainer
formats.text: Faceless voiceover over B-roll and graphics. Allows deep policy dives without being on camera, but needs heavy scripting.

formats.name: Vox populi
formats.text: Street interviews. Very authentic, but you give up some control over the narrative.

steps.title: Strategy, psychology and technical tactics
bullets: **The Lookout Mindset:** social listening. Scan news feeds, comment sections, and pop and online culture to spot existing attention you can hijack.
**Steelmanning:** anticipate the strongest version of your opponent's argument and address it. AI tools can help test counter-points.
**The Trojan horse:** humour and memes slip past audience defences to deliver a political idea.
**Relatability (Wojak / "literally me"):** show genuine emotion, stay unpolished, speak directly to "you".
**Confrontation:** content with a clear opponent is shared twice as much. Direct, bold honesty ("pouring pure wine") builds trust.
warnings: Put the hook on screen as a caption in seconds 1–3. Write descriptions as teasers with relevant keywords and hashtags.
Never film while driving or biking.
Watch out for shadowbanning on war, violence or sensitive conflicts (e.g. Israel/Palestine). Use coded language ("algospeak") when necessary.

steps.title: Group activity: scripting a vertical activist video

activity.intro: In groups of 3–4, draft a script and storyboard for a 60-second vertical video on a civic or social issue.

steps.title: Pick a format
steps.text: Choose one from the taxonomy, e.g. dialogue, satire or explainer.

steps.title: Add a Trojan horse
steps.text: A trend, humour or a pop-culture reference.

steps.title: Name the opponent
steps.text: Identify a clear opponent or counter-argument and steelman it.

steps.title: End with a CTA
steps.text: A concrete, actionable call to action.

activity.note: Each group pitches its concept to the class in 90 seconds. Would the first 3 seconds stop you from scrolling?

steps.title: Reflection and closing
prompts: How do we balance drama-bait or confrontation with ethical, truthful messaging?
How can activists discuss heavily moderated political issues without getting their accounts penalised?
steps.keyMessage: Review the technical don'ts (audio quality, safety, caption placement). Consistency beats perfection in short-form.

materials.name: Slides: mobile stats, horizontal vs. vertical, video taxonomy, memes (Wile E. Coyote, Trojan Horse, Wojak, Labubu)
Downloaded clip examples for each of the 6 formats
Scripting template: format, 3-second hook, trend hijack, core message / steelman, CTA
Platform spec cheat sheet: lengths, caption safe zones, keyword tips for TikTok, Reels, Shorts
Laptop, projector, speakers and participants' smartphones

evaluation: **Formative:** during the taxonomy input, participants identify the formats of sample videos.
**Practical:** scripting worksheets are checked for correct use of Hook → Core → CTA and Trojan horse strategies.
**Peer review:** oral feedback on pitches. Would the first 3 seconds stop a user from scrolling?
